Neugebauer, the co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi Inc., has issued a statement in response to the company's decision to drop its lawsuit against him, which was filed to validate a 70% supermajority bylaw amendment. The lawsuit's dismissal comes after a Texas Business Court ordered Fermi to produce documents and testimony explaining the rationale for the bylaw amendment, and Neugebauer claims that the company's actions confirm that the bylaw move was about entrenching the board's power rather than good governance. Neugebauer's claims challenging the validity of the bylaw remain alive and he will continue to pursue discovery and depositions of key players.

general.summary: Surging pharmaceutical exports led by Novo Nordisk A/S are set to propel Denmark’s economy to its strongest pace in five years and continue fueling the expansion in 2027, according to the country’s largest lender.

general.title: Thailand Must Double Per-Capita Growth to Reach Rich Goal, World Bank Says
general.summary: Thailand needs to more than double the pace of per-capita economic growth to achieve its goal of high-income status by 2037, according to the World Bank, a target it says is within reach if Bangkok pushes through reforms to boost productivity and competitiveness.

general.title: One in Three Firms Backed by UK Covid Fund Are Now Insolvent
general.summary: More than a third of companies backed by the UK government under a rescue program during Covid have gone bust, costing the taxpayer £423 million ($571 million).

general.title: Dry Bulk Shipping Rates Surge on Tight Capesize Vessel Supply
general.summary: A key measure of bulk-shipping rates has touched a two-year high and risks climbing further, according to analysts, as bad weather crimps the availability of Capesize vessels just as exporters ramp up delivery.

general.title: Yen Rallies as Intervention Risk Weighs on Minds of Wary Traders
general.summary: The yen jumped sharply for a second day, reversing a month of gradual decline, as traders lifted bets on Japanese interest-rate hikes and were on high alert to the risk of authorities wading back into the market to boost the currency.
